ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows rhombus ABCD with AD as the bottom base and BC as the top side. Point P lies on segment AD, and a vertical segment BP is drawn from B down to P. A right-angle marker at P shows BP is perpendicular to AD. Reasoning: Since P lies on AD with AP = 3 and PD = 2, the full base length is AD = AP + PD = 3 + 2 = 5. Because ABCD is a rhombus, all sides are equal, so AB = AD = 5. Triangle ABP is right because BP is perpendicular to AD, with hypotenuse AB = 5 and leg AP = 3. By the Pythagorean theorem, BP = sqrt(5^2 - 3^2) = sqrt(25 - 9) = sqrt(16) = 4. The area of the rhombus is base times height, so area = AD × BP = 5 × 4 = 20.

method.method_draft: Use a side-angle formulation for the rhombus. From AP=3 and PD=2, the side length AD is 5, hence AB=5 because ABCD is a rhombus. In right triangle ABP, the projection of AB onto AD is AP=3, so cos(angle DAB)=AP/AB=3/5. Therefore sin(angle DAB)=4/5. The area of a rhombus with side length s and included angle theta is s^2 sin theta, so the area is 5^2·(4/5)=20.
